chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'O Zurara! Open the Adhan with four Takbirs, and conclude it with two Takbirs and two Tahliils.'

key_terms.تَهْلِيلَاتٍ: Declarations of 'There is no god but God' (Tahlil)

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed number of Takbirs and Tahlils at the beginning and end of the Adhan according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the specific ritual structure of the Adhan, emphasizing the prominence of the Takbir (four at the start, two at the end) and the concluding Tahlil. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of adhering to the Prophetic practice as transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing the Adhan's liturgical rhythm from the Iqamah. This structure underscores the theological centrality of God's greatness and oneness in the transition to communal prayer.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said:
‘O Zurara! Open the Azān with exclamations of four Takbīrs, and end it with exclamations of two Takbīrs and two Extollations (of Oneness)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Flammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said, ‘O Zurarah,
begin Adhan with four Takbir (Allah is great beyond description) and end it with two Takbir (Allah is great beyond description) and two Tahlil, (no one deserves worship except Allah).”’
